title: Kaiserschmarrn: Fluffy Torn Caramelised Pancake with Plum Compote
summary: A soufflé-light pancake with raisins, torn into pieces and tossed in caramel, served with a quick plum compote.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Make the compote
steps.text: Cook the plums, sugar, water, lemon juice and cinnamon stick if using in the saucepan over medium-low heat for 15-20 min, stirring from time to time, until the fruit collapses into a thick, jammy sauce. Leave to cool and remove the cinnamon.

steps.title: Soak the raisins
steps.text: Cover the raisins with the warm water or apple juice for 15 min so they plump, then drain.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk the flour and salt with the yolks, vanilla and about a third of the milk into a smooth paste, then whisk in the remaining milk. Starting with a paste avoids lumps.

steps.title: Whip the whites
steps.text: Whisk the egg whites until foamy, then add the 40 g sugar gradually and keep whisking to soft, glossy peaks. Fold into the batter in two goes; the whites make the pancake rise and stay fluffy.

steps.title: Cook the first side
steps.text: Melt half the butter in the frying pan over medium heat until foaming. Pour in all the batter and scatter the raisins over it. Cook for 5-6 min, rotating the pan now and then, until the underside is well browned and the edges have set.

steps.title: Quarter and flip
steps.text: Cut the pancake into quarters with a spatula and turn each piece over; it will be messy, which is fine. Slide the rest of the butter under the edges and cook for 3-4 min until browned underneath.

steps.title: Tear into pieces
steps.text: With the two spatulas, pull the pancake apart into rough 3-4 cm pieces and keep tossing for 1-2 min until no wet batter remains.

steps.title: Caramelise
steps.text: Push the pieces to one side, sprinkle the 2 tbsp sugar over the empty part of the pan and let it melt to light amber, then quickly toss the pieces through it. Dust with icing sugar and serve at once with the plum compote.

tips: A common mistake is over-whipping the whites until stiff and dry; soft peaks fold in more easily and rise better.
Work fast once the sugar starts to caramelise, as it burns quickly.
If the pan is smaller than 28 cm, cook the batter in two batches.
Stewed apples or apple sauce are also traditional alongside.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best eaten straight from the pan. The compote keeps in a covered jar in the fridge for up to 5 days.
